messages:
oliver: Quick sync: we observed tenant A hitting a quota cap in dedicated and runtime auto-failed to hosted despite manifest specifying quota-aware routing. Thread to decide exact admission contract.

nina: can you summarize the failure mode?

oliver: runtime sees dedicated pool full, asks controlplane for fallthrough policy. controlplane returned hosted fallback immediately. But because tenant had reserved tokens in dedicated (soft quota), we should have queued or back-pressured client rather than silently bounce to hosted. Client experienced inconsistent billing and model mismatch.

peter: we currently treat capacity_unavailable as binary: if capacity==0 -> fallback. Need finer states: capacity_soft_exhausted (queueable) vs capacity_hard_exhausted (non-recoverable).

oliver: proposal: change the handshake contract so controlplane returns an admission_decision object for each request path: {decision: "accept|queue|fallback|reject", reason:"...", estimated_wait_seconds: n}. Runtime must honor 'queue' by returning 429 Retry-After or opening a short-lived hold in place.

nina: sketch header shapes: ```
X-Admission-Decision: queue;wait=15
X-Admission-Reason: soft_quota_exhausted
```
runtime returns 429 + body {"retry_after":15,"decision":"queue"} or if fallback allowed then include X-Allowed-Fallbacks list.

peter: tradeoffs: queue increases tail latency and holds resources. But it preserves tenant semantics and billing predictability. Maybe make queuing opt-in in tenant manifest: spec.fallback.queue_on_soft_quota: true/false (default false). If true controlplane will prefer queue over hosted fallback for soft quota.

quota-bot: alert: 6521234568 - tenant_A soft_quota spikes -> 78% of requests would have been queued if enabled.

nina: implement detail: controlplane must return two things in probe response: admission_decision and allowed_fallbacks array with variant metadata. Example probe response snippet (conceptual): ```
200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "admission_decision":"queue",
  "estimated_wait":12,
  "allowed_fallbacks":[{"mode":"hosted","variants":["gptx-8k-quant"]}]
}
```
runtime will then surface to client per manifest rules.

oliver: runtime should include X-Admission-Decision on forwarded requests so downstream logs correlate. Also emit metric admission.decision.{accept,queue,fallback,reject} with tenant_handle tag.

peter: enforce policy: if manifest.spec.fallback.strict_billing=true then fallback to hosted must include explicit tenant consent (notification) and never be silent. Controlplane must emit controlplane.event.fallback_approved with approver="auto|owner". Default is auto.

nina: UX: when queue decision is returned, SDKs should implement exponential backoff with jitter and use Retry-After. For streaming calls we should provide a short-lived hold token so connection can be resumed when capacity frees: X-Hold-Token: <opaque>. Resume flow: client reconnects with X-Resume-Hold: <opaque>. Valid for ≤30s.

ops-bot: runbook link: https://redwood-internal/rr/runbooks/quota-queueing

quota-bot: metric: 6521234570 - 45% of queued attempts eventually accepted within 20s in staging.

oliver: security note: hold tokens must not grant privileges and must be single-use. Also redact tokens in logs.

peter: owners: controlplane (nina) to implement admission_decision contract + probe response changes; runtime (oliver) to honor queue/fallback/reject and surface headers; sdk (peter) to add Retry-After + resume hold behavior.

nina: rollout plan: 1) schema PR for manifest fields spec.fallback.queue_on_soft_quota and spec.fallback.strict_billing 2) probe contract RFC + lightweight JSON response 3) runtime PR + canary: enable queueing for 10% tenants in dedicated pools 4) SDK patch to handle 429/hold token 5) dashboard for admission.decision metrics.

oliver: can we make default behavior conservative (no queue) to avoid unexpected latency?

nina: yes default queue_on_soft_quota=false. We'll flip on opt-in tenants only at canary.

peter: small nit: include estimated_wait_seconds in metric as a histogram to track accuracy.

ops-bot: scheduled canary window placeholder: next Fri 02:00-06:00 UTC.

oliver: I'll prototype runtime hold token logic and add tests for single-use semantics.

nina: I'll start the probe RFC and manifest schema PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
